biur-halacha/1:_: Oath that one will not eat matzah on Passover night — see in Mor U'Ketzia who wrote that if one said he will not eat this matzah, it is forbidden even if he has no other matzah, and they annul his oath for him. And know that if he said he will not eat any matzah of Passover, the oath takes effect inclusively per the view of most poskim, even though he mentioned Passover explicitly; and therefore one should examine per those poskim that the time for eating matzah is from the Torah only until midnight — if so, when one says he will not eat matzah on Passover night, behold he includes the time of exemption with the time of obligation and the oath takes effect inclusively and it is not a vain oath, unless we strain to say that since he mentioned matzah of Passover night his intent is only on the hour when people fulfill the mitzvah of matzah and not afterward — and that is strained, for per that view he would be permitted to eat after midnight; this requires further study.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (א) On Passover night, etc. — but if he said Konam upon me on Passover night, it is forbidden, for a vow takes effect on a matter of mitzvah; see Yoreh De'ah siman 239. Bach wrote: one who swore he will not eat maror or will not drink the four cups on Passover night — since it is d'rabbanan, his oath takes effect and we compel him to request annulment of his oath; and if he swore affirmatively, we do not compel him, but it is fitting he should request annulment of his oath.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (א) [Seif 1] He said an oath that he will not eat matzah, etc. — and the reason is because the oath came to nullify the mitzvah of sit and do not do inclusively; therefore this oath, since it takes effect on matzah of the whole year, also takes effect on matzah of Passover night — Beit Yosef in the name of Ran. Taz seif kaf alef. Magen Avraham seif kaf alef. Chayei Adam letter alef.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Seif alef — matzah without specification is forbidden to eat. And one who says an oath that he will not eat in the sukkah of mitzvah — even though all seven days except the first night are permission, we do not say since it takes effect on the rest of the days, for on the rest of the days it also does not take effect, for even though he can eat casually outside the sukkah, nevertheless since he eats fixed meals in the sukkah it is a mitzvah and is called swearing to nullify the mitzvah — Tashbetz part 1 siman 100. And in Chokhmat Shlomo that also on the eighth they sit — if so the language "sukkah of mitzvah" includes the eighth as well; and one may say it is inclusive since it takes effect on the eighth — this requires further study.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: Forbidden — Ba'er Hetev; and see in Shach Choshen Mishpat siman 73 seif kaf yud alef who wrote the reason that inclusion helps here to nullify the mitzvah, for in the middle of the year the obligation of matzah and sukkah has not yet applied to him at all — see there in Taz in Hagahat Chacham Tzvi; one may say he challenged Shach on this and wrote that if one said matzah without specification, even if standing on Passover nights it is forbidden to eat, etc. — see there; and see in the Acharonim there who wrote to reconcile Shach's words; and see in Kaf HaChayyim to Sefer Ketubot in Even HaEzer siman 218. (And I wrote there that initially it was difficult for me what Chacham Tzvi wrote from Tosafot Shevuot — Shach is not dealing with the matter of the essence of the oath taking effect, for regarding that there is no place for Shach's distinction, for now there is no mitzvah; nevertheless when we judge the oath's taking effect on Passover nights, then it is already a mitzvah; therefore Tosafot needed to divide on another matter, to say the oath takes effect only regarding whether one must fulfill the oath or must fulfill the mitzvah he is sworn and standing upon; and in truth the punishment of the oath depends on which preceded — Shach wrote regarding matzah that since there is no obligation now, the oath preceded when there was no obligation, and when the obligation arrives the oath's taking effect was already — therefore Shach did not mention from Tosafot Shevuot at all, for they deal with the essence of oath taking effect, and the matters are clear as I explained in its place, and here I shortened. And what Ketzot HaChoshen wrote — Ra'avad's words in Temim De'im — Kaf HaChayyim brought here, and this is not Shach's intent; also what he wrote that Rav R' Chasdai in responsa of Rivash is like Ra'avad — it is not so, as explained in responsa of Rivash, for it is explained there his reason is because even though it includes on what is not mitzvah, nevertheless the essence of the oath is on a matter of mitzvah, and he brings an oath not to eat matzah on Passover night — even though it includes entirely, nevertheless the essence of the oath is on matzah of mitzvah, and this Rivash rejected there — see there; and also the proof from an oath not to sleep, etc. is astonishing, for there since the oath he uttered cannot be fulfilled it is void entirely, unlike there where one swore not to sleep, etc.; and likewise in matzah, for we hold that on a matter that is not mitzvah it takes effect well — one may say that through inclusion it takes effect also on mitzvah, and in this Ran and Rivash deal, and I explained well in its place, there's help.)
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Magen Avraham seif kaf alef — matzah without specification, because it is an inclusive prohibition since it takes effect, etc. — so it should read.
